newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher but strong mood turning.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher but strong mood turning.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose Thursday but traders and analysts said the market was showing an increasingly uncertain mood.
"Good news is not making the market rally. I am kind of skeptical," said an analyst at a foreign bank.
Peso bonds surged earlier in the week after the government announced Wednesday it issued a 10-year 500 million peso bond in international markets. That rally fizzled Thursday.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 125.75, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 89-1/2.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose just 0.05 peso to 100.40.
Creeping suspicions the U.S. Treasuries could turn lower was also holding the market back.

"Latin Brady's are mildly higher, but retain a slightly broader consolidative tone awaiting directional influence from Treasuries," said analysts at MMS International in an investor note. "...direction will be decided by U.S. bonds or stocks. But February is a month to be careful in."
Call money rates fell to 5.15 percent from 5.20 percent.
